diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ be nonzero, $m\geq n$, and $\Vert A\Vert^{-1}A=U^\top V$ be the decomposition given in Lemma \ref{lem:orthogonal_decomposition}.
Any matrix $A\in \f R^{m\times n}$ of spectral norm 1 and $m\ge n$ can be decomposed as $A=U^\top V$

issues.failure_explanation: The cited reduction is proved only for a nonzero m by n matrix with m>=n. The corollary starts from an arbitrary biclique matrix M in R^{m x n}; when m<n, the decomposition lemma and reduction theorem are being applied without their dimensional hypothesis. The same value is obtained after transposing the instance, SV(-M,R^m_+,R^n_+)=SV(-M^T,R^n_+,R^m_+), or by a padding argument, but the proof does not say this.

failure_location.quote: Let $M\in\R^{m\times n}$ with at least one positive entry. In Theorem \ref{th:SVcones_NPhard} it is shown that $\PSV(-M)=\SV(-M,\R^m_+,\R^n_+)$ is NP-hard.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the transpose/padding sentence before invoking Theorem th:reduction_SVcones_anglescones so the instance satisfies m>=n.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of NP-hardness of MA(P,Q) has an unhandled rectangular case m<n as written; the statement itself is recoverable with a one-line reduction to m>=n.
issues.title: NP-hardness corollary for angles uses the reduction outside its stated m>=n hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The missing case is repaired by transposing or padding the instance; no rate, guarantee, or advertised NP-hardness conclusion is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let  $A_x:=\ol H^+ A^\top\ol G$,  $A_y:=\ol G^+ A\ol H$
$M := \begin{pmatrix} 0& \ol H^+ A^\top\ol G\\\ol G^+ A\ol H& 0 \end{pmatrix}$

issues.failure_explanation: For z=[y;x], the necessary eigenproblem uses top-right block H^+A^TG and bottom-left block G^+AH. The algorithm instead forms A_y=G^+A^TH and A_x=H^+AG; the second product is even dimensionally invalid for rectangular A unless A is replaced by A^T. Thus for general rectangular A and non-orthonormal generators BFAS solves a different eigenproblem than the one justified by Theorem th:critical_points_SVcones and Proposition pro:sufficient_conditions_feasibility.

failure_location.quote: \State $ A_y = \ol G^+ A^\top \ol H$, $A_x = \ol H^+A \ol G$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define A_y=ol G^+ A ol H and A_x=ol H^+ A^\top ol G, swapping the product choice when |I|>|J|, exactly as in Proposition pro:sufficient_conditions_feasibility.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised exactness guarantee of BFAS for general SV(A,G,H) is not supported as written; the angle case A=I and orthonormal-generator experiments do not expose the swap.
issues.title: BFAS active-set eigenproblem uses A and A^T in the wrong places
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of two matrix definitions to match the already-proved necessary conditions; no new proof architecture or loss of the exactness claim is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let us denote this projection $x = \mathcal P_+(c)$.

issues.failure_explanation: For c=Av with some negative entry, min(c,0) is nonpositive, so the printed x is nonpositive and is not feasible for x>=0; it also gives <x,c>=+||min(c,0)|| rather than the minimum -||min(c,0)||. The minimizing feasible vector is the normalized positive part of -c.

failure_location.quote: It can be easily checked that the optimal solution is $x = \frac{\min(c,0)}{\|\min(c,0)\|}$ if $c \ngeq 0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace min(c,0) by max(-c,0) in the projection, equivalently x=max(-c,0)/||max(-c,0)|| when c is not nonnegative.
issues.overall_effect: The closed-form P=R_+^m update used by E-AO would return an infeasible iterate and the wrong objective value for PSV/biclique runs.
issues.title: Orthant subproblem projection in E-AO has the wrong sign
issues.why_classification: This is a one-sign correction; the supplementary notes already contain the corrected formula, and the heuristic framework is unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\wt P=UP$ and $\wt Q=VQ$ are closed convex cones in $\f R^{m+s}$ that are isometrically equivalent to $P,Q$.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the lift, <Uu,Vv>=<u,Av>/||A||=sigma/||A||. Hence a (P,Q)-singular value sigma corresponds to a lifted critical angle arccos(sigma/||A||), not arccos(sigma); the printed version is also undefined when sigma<-1 for ||A||>1.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, $\sigma$ is a $(P,Q)$-singular value of $A$ if and only if $\arccos(\sigma)$ is a critical angle between $\wt P$ and $\wt Q$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change arccos(sigma) to arccos(sigma/||A||) in the remark.
issues.overall_effect: Only the interpretive remark is wrong; the reduction theorem and NP-hardness corollary are unaffected.
issues.title: Lifted-angle remark drops the division by ||A||
issues.why_classification: A single scaling correction restores the statement, with no effect on the proved reduction or later algorithms.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the optimal value of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ is the minimum entry of $G^\top A H$

issues.failure_explanation: One generator on each side with a nonnegative 1 by 1 matrix [c] is not sufficient for the optimal value to equal ||A||; for example P=Q=span(e_1) and A=diag(0,2) gives c=0 while ||A||=2. The correct check is that the single entry equals ||A||, or more generally compare min_{i,j}(G^TAH)_{ij} with ||A||.

failure_location.quote: However, the case $\langle u, Av\rangle = \Vert A\Vert$ is easy to check, since it is equivalent to say that both $P,Q$ have only one generator and $G^\top AH$ is a $1\times 1$ nonnegative matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add that the 1 by 1 entry must equal ||A||, or replace the sentence by the minimum-entry check from Proposition pro:nonnegative_case_SVcones.
issues.overall_effect: This standalone preprocessing claim is false as written, although the surrounding Case 1/Case 2 tests can still be implemented by comparing the computed optimum with ||A||.
issues.title: The lambda*=+||A|| check is stated as a false equivalence
issues.why_classification: The missing equality condition is local and does not change the polynomial-time preprocessing scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: if $N = Q\Lambda Q^\top$ is the eigendecomposition of $N$, then $P =Q\Lambda^-Q^\top = Q(Q^\top NQ)^-Q^\top$

issues.failure_explanation: Minimizing <U,V> over U psd with ||U||_F=1 is projection of -V onto the PSD cone. With V=Q Sigma Q^T, that projection is Q max(-Sigma,0) Q^T, equivalently -Q min(Sigma,0)Q^T; the printed Q min(0,Sigma)Q^T is generally not psd and has the wrong sign.

failure_location.quote: The optimal $U = Q \min(0,\Sigma) Q^\top$ where $V = Q \Sigma Q^\top$ is an eigendecomposition of $V$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Q min(0,Sigma)Q^T by Q max(-Sigma,0)Q^T.
issues.overall_effect: The supplementary closed form for the PSD subproblem is incorrect; using it would not produce the projected PSD matrix.
issues.title: Closed-form PSD projection in the extra material has the wrong sign
issues.why_classification: A sign correction gives the standard PSD projection; no algorithmic guarantee or rate is altered.
